name: Colour Rulebook
summary: Colour strategy, roles, OKLCH, contrast and dark mode.
check: Make a contrast table of every text/background pair in light and dark.
View the site with a colour-blindness simulator (DevTools Rendering panel).

rules.title: Pick a colour strategy before picking colours
rules.text: One of: **Restrained** (tinted neutrals plus one accent; the default for product UI), **Committed** (one strong colour covers 30–60 % of the surface), **Full palette** (three or four named roles), **Drenched** (the surface is the colour). Write the choice into the decisions record.

rules.title: Light or dark is decided, never defaulted
rules.text: Write one sentence about where the site is used (who, where, under what light) and let it decide. Neither mode is the safe choice.

rules.title: Colours come from the subject
rules.text: Take them from the product, its photography, its materials or its place, not from a generic palette generator. See `SL-01`, `SL-64` to `SL-67`.

rules.title: Roles, not swatches
rules.text: Name colours by job: `bg`, `surface`, `surface-raised`, `text`, `text-muted`, `border`, `accent`, `accent-contrast`, `focus`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`. Components use roles, never raw values.

rules.title: Define colours in OKLCH
rules.text: `oklch()` keeps lightness steps even across hues, so ramps and dark-mode variants are predictable. Keep sRGB fallbacks only where old browsers matter.

rules.title: Tint the neutrals
rules.text: Greys lean slightly towards the brand hue (chroma about 0.005–0.02). Pure `#000` and `#fff` are rarely the right ground; near-black and off-white are.

rules.title: A small palette
rules.text: About 8–12 tokens for a marketing site, a few more for an app with states. Fewer opacities and fewer shades (`SL-07`).

rules.title: One meaning per colour
rules.text: If the accent means "you can click this", do not use it for decoration or static text. Status colours mean status only.

rules.title: Contrast table before building
rules.text: Check every text/background pair you will use: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text (about 24 px, or 19 px bold), icons and control borders, 7:1 for small text when possible. Check both themes and hover/disabled states.

rules.title: Colour as the only signal
rules.text: Errors, status, chart series and required fields also carry a label, icon, pattern or shape. Check with a colour-blindness simulation.

rules.title: Grey text on coloured backgrounds
rules.text: Muted grey on a coloured surface drops contrast; use a tint of the surface colour or white/near-black at a checked ratio.

rules.title: Dark mode is redesigned, not inverted
rules.text: Dim, slightly tinted grounds; raised surfaces get lighter, not shadowed; accents usually lose a little chroma and gain lightness; body text is off-white, not pure white. Large white areas in images are softened.

rules.title: Follow the system setting
rules.text: Respect `prefers-color-scheme`; add a manual switch only when people ask for it, and remember their choice. Support `prefers-contrast: more` with stronger borders and text.

rules.title: Elevation in dark mode is lighter, not darker
rules.text: Each raised layer (card, popover, dialog) is a step lighter than the one below.

rules.title: Accent sparingly
rules.text: The primary action, links, the current selection and focus. Not every icon, heading and border (`DC-11`).

rules.title: Respect culture and context
rules.text: Red can mean danger, loss or luck; green can mean gain or not. In charts and finance follow the audience's convention, and label the meaning.

rules.title: Define state colours once
rules.text: Success, warning, danger and info are tokens with a background, border and text variant each, checked for contrast in both themes.

rules.title: A visible focus colour
rules.text: The focus ring has its own token with 3:1 contrast against every surface it can appear on, not the accent at low opacity.

rules.title: Red and green as the only difference
rules.text: Never rely on a red/green pair alone for good and bad, up and down, or valid and invalid; add a sign, icon or label (`CL-10`).

rules.title: Several saturated accents in one view
rules.text: One saturated accent per view. A second strong colour competes with the primary action.

rules.title: Pure black text on pure white for long reading
rules.text: For long reading, soften the extremes slightly (near-black on off-white) to reduce glare, while keeping contrast well above 7:1.
